mechanism: Ethambutol may increase mycophenolate levels through potential inhibition of UGT enzymes responsible for mycophenolate glucuronidation, and both drugs can cause overlapping gastrointestinal and hematologic effects.
action: Monitor for mycophenolate toxicity (gastrointestinal symptoms, myelosuppression) and consider therapeutic drug monitoring of mycophenolic acid levels if clinically feasible; adjust mycophenolate dose if toxicity develops.
